paper.title: Fast mmwave Beam Alignment via Correlated Bandit Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Beam alignment as a stochastic MAB with correlated (multimodal) reward function over the beam space
unmapped: N beams mapped to the region X=[0,1]; the analysis treats the normalized reward as a function f on [0,1] (X-armed / HOO-style)
weak Lipschitz condition only around the optimum: f* - f(x) <= c_H ||x* - x||^alpha
dissimilarity q(x,y)=w||x-y||^beta with bounded-diameter and well-shaped hierarchical partition (Assumption 2)
the learner knows the noise variance sigma^2 (prior knowledge of the channel fluctuation)
settings.definition_quote: we assume that the reward follows a Gaussian distribution with a variance $\sigma^2$. In other words, $\sigma^2$ also represents the variance of the channel fluctuation, which is utilized as \emph{prior knowledge} in the following algorithm design.

tuning: E-value confidence margin sqrt(2 sigma^2 log t / N) + rho_1 gamma^h

source.label: lemma:expected_N_bound
source.quote: For any node $(h,j)$ whose suboptimality is larger than $\rho_1 \gamma^h$, the expected number of times that $(h,j)$ has been visited until time slot $T$, is upper bounded by $\mathbb{E}\left[N_{h,j}(T)\right] \leq\frac{8\sigma^2 \log T}{\left(\epsilon_{h,j} -\rho_1 \gamma^h\right)^2}+c$ where $c$ is a constant.

results.notes: Bound on expected number of visits of a suboptimal node, not regret. c is an unspecified constant (mapped to c_alg).

conditions: Assumption 1 (weak Lipschitz around optimum with exponent alpha)
alpha = beta so that kappa = 1/beta - 1/alpha = 0 (smoothness known); general case gives O(T^((kappa+1)/(kappa+2)) (log T)^(1/(kappa+2)))
tuning: rho_1 > 0, gamma in (0,1) matching the bounded-diameter assumption

source.label: theorem: regret_bound
source.quote: The upper bound on the cumulative regret of HBA is $R^\pi\left({T}\right)=O\left(\sqrt{T\log T}\right).$

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards (pseudo-regret). Proof gives O(T^{(kappa+1)/(kappa+2)} (log T)^{1/(kappa+2)}) and sets kappa=0. Constants hidden; regret analysis follows HOO (Bubeck et al.). Algorithm uses log t, so treated as anytime though the proof uses T.
